findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses AND instead of OR
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, so a user must be both admin and owner to pass. A team admin who is not the owner, or a team owner who is not an admin, is denied, and the OR-style permission intent in the name is not implemented. The check should be `||`.

findings.title: Calendar attendees are updated with the requester's credentials, not the organizer's
findings.body: The `EventManager` is built from `ctx.user` and that user's credentials (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`). Any authorized actor (a team admin, or an attendee) triggers the calendar update through their own calendar, while the event lives on the organizer's calendar. The update should use the booking organizer's user and credentials, which are already loaded as `booking.user`.

findings.title: Duplicate emails within the input are not removed and get inserted twice
findings.body: `uniqueGuests` only filters out emails that already exist as attendees and blacklisted emails. If the `guests` array contains the same address twice (the schema does not enforce uniqueness, and the dialog check is client-side only), both copies are passed to `createMany`, creating duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails.

findings.title: Blacklist check is case-sensitive while the blacklist is lowercased
findings.body: The blacklist entries are lowercased on line 71, but `guest` is compared as-is on line 77. An input like `Blocked@Example.com` bypasses a blacklist entry `blocked@example.com`. Email comparison should be normalized on both sides.

findings.title: Attendees are persisted before calendar update, with no rollback on failure
findings.body: The attendee rows are written to the database (lines 92-106), then `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` runs outside any try/catch (line 165). If the calendar call throws, the mutation fails with an error, but the guests are already saved, so the UI reports failure while the data has changed and the calendar is out of sync. The DB write and calendar update need to be reconciled or the calendar error handled.

findings.title: Email sending receives raw input instead of the filtered guest list
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the original `guests` input rather than `uniqueGuests`. Guests who were already attendees are classified as new and receive the 'you are scheduled' email. Blacklisted or duplicate addresses are also passed through, and the function treats them as new guests.

findings.title: Email failures are swallowed with no error detail logged
findings.body: The `catch` logs only the static string 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails' and discards `err`, so the actual failure is lost. It also uses `console.log` instead of the project logger used elsewhere in this codebase.

findings.title: Any existing attendee can add arbitrary guests to a booking
findings.body: The authorization check allows any booking attendee (matched by session email) to add guests, with no restriction on booking status or time. Cancelled or past bookings are also not excluded. Each addition triggers emails to the organizer, team members and all attendees, which allows spam or abuse of the booking's recipient list. The permission model should be confirmed and restricted to the organizer and admins if attendees should not have this capability.

findings.title: No limit on the number of guests per request
findings.body: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no max length and no uniqueness constraint. A single call can insert and email an unbounded number of addresses, which is an abuse and cost vector for the email provider.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails event-type metadata
findings.body: Every other send function in this file gates host and attendee emails with `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` and the `hostEmailDisabled` / `attendeeEmailDisabled` flags. This function takes neither and always sends to organizer, team members and attendees. Hosts who disabled standard emails on the event type will still receive these notifications.

findings.title: Subject uses attendees[0].name, which is often empty for new guests
findings.body: New guests are created with `name: ""`. If the first attendee in the list is a newly added guest, the subject is built with an empty name (e.g. 'Guests Added: X with  at ...'). The subject should use the organizer or the booking's primary attendee.

findings.title: Recipient header is malformed when attendee name is empty
findings.body: `to` is built as `${this.attendee.name} <${this.attendee.email}>`. Guests are created with an empty name, which produces ' <guest@example.com>' with a leading space and no display name. Falling back to the bare email when the name is empty would avoid this.

findings.title: Hardcoded English tooltip text bypasses i18n
findings.body: `<Tooltip content="Remove email">` is a literal string, while the rest of the component uses `t(...)`. Non-English users see English text, and the project's translation pipeline does not cover it.

findings.title: Closing the dialog via overlay or Escape does not reset the entered emails
findings.body: Only the Cancel button resets `multiEmailValue` and `isInvalidEmail`. Dismissing via `onOpenChange` (overlay click, Escape) keeps the previous input and the validation error, so the next open shows stale state.

findings.title: Fallback in error toast is dead code
findings.body: `message` is a template string that always contains the separator, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never falls back. The intended fallback is never shown on errors with no code.
